title.title: Stable blowup for a defocusing Schrödinger equation
title.subtitle: Claim: an open set of smooth data on the 12-dimensional torus blows up in finite time

plain: A wave equation with a repelling force can still blow up, and not by fluke: nearby starts blow up too

object.heading: Schematic: the size of $u$ at the blowup point; dashed: nearby data

beats.text: Defocusing NLS on $\mathbb{T}^{12}$: in high dimension, energy no longer controls regularity
Earlier blowups needed a thin set of data. Here every nearby datum blows up too
So smooth random data blow up with positive probability

steps: Take a large power: the blowup profile becomes a flat core
Certify its spectrum exactly, then move from all space to a torus
A degree argument turns one blowup into an open set of them

achievement.label: Defocusing NLS: blowup on an open set of data
achievement.context: Before: blowup only on thin, non-generic data (Merle–Raphaël–Rodnianski–Szeftel, 2022)
achievement.note: For some odd power $p$, arbitrarily large: not every large $p$

verify.detail: Lean: stable blowup and the random-data corollary, about 191,000 lines
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean

voice.text: Defocusing waves in twelve dimensions. Earlier blowups needed a thin set of data.
Take a large power, certify the spectrum exactly, then use a degree argument.
Claimed: blowup on an open set of data.

sources.quote: There is an open set of data on the 12-dimensional torus that blows up in self-similar fashion, so random data blow up with positive probability.

sources.quote: Merle, Raphaël, Rodnianski and Szeftel showed smooth data can blow up (Inventiones 2022), but only on a thin, non-generic set of data.
